hook.text: A spreadsheet shows $5 million in revenue. But the hidden cells and formula history tell a different story.

buildup.text: Spreadsheet forensics examines formulas, cell histories, hidden rows, and metadata in Excel files.

discovery.text: Metadata reveals who created the file, when it was modified, and what changes were made.

twist.text: Deleted cells can be recovered. Overwritten formulas can be traced. Spreadsheets have long memories.

climax.text: A single altered formula in a financial model can misstate millions—and forensic tools can find it.

punchline.text: The spreadsheet remembers every change you made.

quiz.question: What can spreadsheet metadata reveal?
options: Who created the file and when it was changed

details.summary: Spreadsheet forensics examines Excel and other spreadsheet files for evidence of manipulation—hidden formulas, deleted cells, modified dates, and intentionally introduced errors. This topic covers how forensic accountants analyze spreadsheets for signs of fraud.
details.whyItMatters: Spreadsheets are where many frauds are planned and concealed. Unlike accounting software with audit trails, spreadsheets can be easily modified without leaving obvious traces unless examined forensically.
takeaways: Hidden rows, columns, and worksheets can conceal data the creator doesn't want others to see
File metadata reveals creation dates, last-modified dates, and authors that may contradict claims
Hardcoded values that override formulas are a common way to manipulate calculated results

faq.question: What do forensic accountants look for when examining spreadsheets?
faq.answer: They check for hidden rows, columns, and sheets; hardcoded values replacing formulas; circular references that produce desired numbers; file metadata inconsistencies; unusual formatting that masks data; and changes tracked through file versioning or metadata analysis.

faq.question: Can deleted or modified spreadsheet data be recovered?
faq.answer: Sometimes. Earlier file versions may exist in cloud storage, email attachments, or backup systems. File metadata can reveal modification history. Forensic tools can sometimes recover previous states from temporary files. Excel's Track Changes feature, if enabled, logs modifications.
